neighbours.label: nouns naming dominant tech companies or platforms as a group (big platforms, the tech giants)
fire: Regulators in Brussels want to rein in the big social media platforms that control online advertising.
Smaller startups struggle to compete with search giants that own the whole advertising market.
The open web has been swallowed by a handful of monopoly platforms built on proprietary apps.
Critics say the dominant tech companies collect far too much data about their users.
Search engines and social networks have become the gatekeepers of online news.
The hearing grilled executives from the largest internet companies about privacy.
Online retail is now dominated by two or three huge e-commerce platforms.
Developers complain that app store owners take a large cut of every sale.
quiet: Regulators in Brussels want to rein in the big supermarket chains that control food prices.
Smaller bakeries struggle to compete with grocery giants that own the whole flour market.
The old high street has been swallowed by a handful of shopping centres built on the edge of town.
Critics say the dominant oil companies pay far too little tax on their profits.
Local newspapers and radio stations used to be the gatekeepers of regional news.
The hearing grilled executives from the largest airline companies about delays.
Coffee sales are now dominated by two or three huge café chains.
Farmers complain that wholesale buyers take a large cut of every sale.
